## What changed

- `packages/omniviewdev-runtime/src/ui/useConnectionMetadata.ts` (new): the curated entry's call, `useConnectionMetadata({ pluginID?, connectionID, enabled? })`, and `UseConnectionMetadataOptions`; it calls the main entry's hook with `enabled ? connectionID : undefined`.
- `packages/omniviewdev-runtime/src/ui/v1.ts`: exports that wrapper and the six types its signature mentions (`ConnectionMetadataState`, `UseConnectionMetadataOptions`, `ConnectionMetadataSnapshot`, `ConnectionMetadataEntry`, `ConnectionMetadataError`, `ConnectionMetadataValue`).
- The main entry (`hooks/connection/useConnectionMetadata.ts` and its test, `docs/plugin-development.md`) is NOT changed: identical to `origin/main`.
- `api/ui-v1.api.md` (regenerated by `pnpm run api:update`; there is no report for the main entry), `src/ui/v1.test.ts` (the written-out list of names; `useConnectionMetadata` joins `ONLY_HERE`: it is no longer the main entry's own function), `src/ui/useConnectionMetadata.test.tsx` (new), `.changeset/ui-v1-connection-metadata.md` (minor; additive to the curated entry only).

## Why this shape (for the reviewer)

- One hook and its type closure, nothing more. `useConnectionMetadataSelector` and `useConnectionMetadataConnections` (many connections) and `readCurrentConnectionMetadataString` are not exported: the plugin reads one connection, and the rule "a stale fact is not a current one" belongs where a page decides, in the words it says it in. Each can be added later under rule 4.
- The freshness is part of the value (`current` / `stale` / `unavailable`), so the types are exported whole: a page that draws a version must say which of the three it has. No helper here flattens them to a string.
- One implementation, two entry shapes: the wrapper calls the main entry's hook, so the host still mounts one cache and one `resource/connection/metadata` event subscription whichever shape a consumer calls (`src/ui/useConnectionMetadata.test.tsx`: the wrapper and the root hook in one render, one `GetConnectionMetadata` call, one subscription, one refresh).
- An older host's entry lacks the name; a plugin that needs it says which host version has it (rule 4). What that does and does not catch is under "Compat of a name".
- **The curated call is an options object**: `useConnectionMetadata({ pluginID?, connectionID, enabled? })`, as `useConnectionReadiness({ pluginID?, connectionID, enabled? })`, `useResources` and `useResolvedResourceTarget` are called. The positional form `(explicitPluginID, connectionID)` has `undefined` mean "off" and would put the implementation's parameter name in the API report; rules 3 and 4 at the head of `ui/v1.ts` freeze a shape once it ships, and the curated entry has no consumer yet, so its shape is chosen now and not after. `connectionID` may be `undefined` (off), `enabled` defaults to true and `false` is off: either reads nothing and subscribes to nothing, and its `refresh` does nothing.
- **Why a wrapper and not a change of the hook** (found by CI, `e2e-application`): the shipped Kubernetes plugin builds against the runtime's ROOT export and calls `useConnectionMetadata('kubernetes', id)` positionally; changing the root hook's signature failed its type check (`TS2554 Expected 1 arguments, but got 2`, at the two call sites above) and would break every plugin that already ships. The first version of this change assumed the hook was unreleased because its changeset is pending; the plugin was built against the repository's runtime all the same. The root hook is a shipped API and stays; the curated entry, which has no consumer yet, gets the shape of its neighbours.
- Not changed: `useResolvedPluginId` prefers a `PluginContext` over the explicit `pluginID` (review N2). `ui-next` mounts none; the existing test "uses plugin context identity instead of an explicit upstream plugin name" holds that rule.

## Compat of a name

A name the curated entry of an OLDER host lacks is `undefined` for a plugin that imports it, not a refusal (review N1 of #723, S1 of #724). What each piece does about the NAMES a plugin imports (as against the specifiers it imports from):

| Piece | Does about names |
|---|---|
| Plugin `hack/vendor-host.sh` | Nothing about names. Vendors `shared-specifiers.json` (`SHARED_SPECIFIERS_V1`: six module names), the packed kit and runtime, and the host commit it came from (`ui/vendor/HOST_COMMIT`). The packed runtime's declarations carry the curated entry's names, so the plugin's `tsc` (`pnpm run build` = `typecheck && vite build && check-bundle`) rejects a name the entry of THAT commit lacks. That is the one check on names, and it is against the vendored commit, not against the host the plugin will run on. |
| Plugin `ui/scripts/check-bundle.mjs` | Specifiers only: the first `System.register` dependency list must be local files or in `shared-specifiers.json`, plus `contributionV1`. It never reads a setter, so it cannot see a name. |
| Host `ui-next/plugins/loader/preflight.ts` (`unservedImports`, called from `importBundle.ts`) | Specifiers only: the same dependency list against `SHARED_SPECIFIERS_V1`, refusing the bundle before it runs with a typed `IncompatibleBundleError`. A name inside `@omniviewdev/runtime/ui/v1` is not looked at. |
| Host `scripts/ui-next-pods/pin.mjs` (`checkPin`, tested in `pin.test.mjs`) | Specifiers and the commit: the plugin's list equals `SHARED_SPECIFIERS_V1`, and `HOST_COMMIT` is the host under test or one of its ancestors. It runs before anything is built and reads no bundle. Because the entry only grows (rule 4, held by the names test and the API report) and the plugin's `tsc` held its names to the entry at `HOST_COMMIT`, an ancestor commit means every name the plugin imports is in the host under test: the pairing it checks is covered, by that chain, not by an enumeration. |
| Host `ui-next/plugins/loader/specifiers.ts`, `shared.ts` | Serve each shared module whole, `async () => import('@omniviewdev/runtime/ui/v1')`, through SystemJS `exportModule`. No list of names exists in the loader. |

**Link time or render time: render (call) time.** SystemJS gives a `system` bundle's setter the module's namespace; the setter copies the names it wants (`V=>{es=V.useConnectionMetadata,ts=V.openLogStream}` is the shape of the Kubernetes plugin's built `entry.js`). A name the registered module lacks is `undefined`, and nothing is checked. Run with the real `systemjs` of this repository, the loader's own registration shape (`System.register('shared://curated', [], …)`, a bundle importing `present` and `absent`): `linked: present=function absent=undefined`, `executed`, then `call: TypeError: absent is not a function`. The review's `r2c-missing-name.mjs` (real host built without #723, a bundle whose Items hook calls the hook) saw the same in the window: `Couldn't load Items / This page failed to display.`, console `TypeError: N is not a function`, contained by the page boundary. I did not rerun the review's script (it builds a host); the node run above is the cheap part of it.

**Where a guard could go, and why none is added here.**

- The gap that matters is a NEW plugin on an OLDER host in the field. A host that lacks the name also lacks any check for it, so no code in this repository can close it. Only a plugin-side or marker-side measure reaches such a host: the plugin guards the call (`typeof useConnectionMetadata === 'function'`) or the plugin says which host it needs and the hosts that read the marker refuse (S1 of #724: a capability marker in the contribution, a decision before the channel where hosts and plugins do not move together). The entry has no "since" record per name, so even a marker needs one to be meaningful. (The curated `useConnectionMetadata` is no longer the main entry's own function, see "Why this shape"; the curated entry's list of names stays held by `v1.test.ts` and the API report.)
- `pin.mjs` already covers the pairing the cluster check runs (chain above); a direct name comparison there would repeat what the ancestry and the plugin's `tsc` already prove, and the plugin's `.tgz` is not unpacked at that point.
- A names check in the loader's preflight (`unservedNames` beside `unservedImports`, refusing with `IncompatibleBundleError` before any line runs) would protect hosts that carry it from a plugin built against a later host. It must read the names from each setter of the minified text (`V=>{a=V.x,b=V.y}`; the parameter is renamed by the minifier; `export *` and namespace use are other shapes) and compare them to the served module's keys, which loads the curated entry at fetch time (HSH-7, `optimisations.md`: nothing is loaded eagerly). A pattern over minified text that refuses a good plugin is worse than the crash it prevents, so it needs a parser and its own hostile-case tests: more than a small change, not added here. It also needs the same decision as the marker. Where it would go: `preflight.ts` and the `fetch` hook in `importBundle.ts`.
- For HM3c: the plugin's landing page calls the hook, so merge this PR before #724 (as the review says), or the plugin guards the call. The plugin repository was not changed.
